useCases.title: Tervion DigiClinic
useCases.summary:
Tervion Etäklinikka is a fictional Finnish telemedicine clinic. A video GP visit, a prescription renewal, or a care record still needs a high-assurance login before the call starts. In the Nordics, that login is usually BankID. A second country means a second national eID and a second contract. A patient who is not Finnish does not have BankID at all.

Tervion is the clinic as a site: six specialities, next GP in nine minutes. The clinic asks Authbound Wallet for given_name, family_name, and kela_card_number, because the record needs the Kela entitlement as well as the person. For foreigners, the requirements would differ. After that, the video room is the next screen. Anna sees the appointment on the dashboard, with two renewals waiting, records bound to that session.

If the visitor has no Kela card in the wallet yet, the demo issues an Authbound ID and a Kela Card first, then runs the same login.

She books Dr. Anni Mäkelä, live in 4 minutes. Login opens: Log in to your clinic record.

Authbound Wallet shows given_name, family_name, and kela_card_number. Anna accepts. If those credentials are missing, the demo issues Authbound ID and a Kela Card first.

The clinic session is live. Logged in securely, Anna. Dr. Mäkelä has your record. The video room opens at 14:20.

useCases.title: Nordhaus: Open a Bank Account
useCases.summary:
Nordhaus is a fictional Nordic retail bank. We built it for the moment every licensed bank already has: you cannot issue an IBAN or a debit card until KYC is signed, and the customer is already halfway out the door.

Today that moment is a liveness vendor and a waiting room. The bank pays per attempt, stores a pile of identity images, and still cannot prove much more than someone uploaded a photo. Drop-off is the product.

We made Nordhaus a full bank front, not a KYC widget, so a product or compliance lead can walk the journey and see the account exist afterwards. Authbound Wallet presents given_name, family_name, birth_date, nationality, and age_over_18. A pass is a signed KYC record. The same sitting mints the Finnish IBAN and the virtual debit, so the money is actually movable. That is the sale: cheaper onboarding, no document warehouse, and a customer who did not bounce.

Accept IBAN FI73 1940 6X24. Activate debit card ending 4827.

useCases.title: Keystone: A signed lease in one sitting
useCases.summary:
Keystone is a fictional Finnish letting marketplace. We built it for the part of renting that still dies in email: prove who you are, prove you can pay, then get a signature that actually holds.

Landlords still collect payslips anyone can edit, chase an HR letter, then either accept a click-to-sign or book a notary. The tenant has already found another flat. Agencies run those as three products. That is why applications stall and why a remote letting never quite closes.

We made Keystone a real listing, not a signature widget, so a landlord or agency can walk the journey and see the lease exist afterwards. Authbound Wallet presents identity, an employer income attestation, and current address. The same sitting signs the lease with a qualified electronic signature, the one that has the legal effect of wet ink. The landlord keeps an audit trail. The tenant gets the keys. Nobody stored a PDF of a payslip.

useCases.title: Gradus: verify the diploma before you interview
useCases.summary:
Gradus is a fictional employer-side hiring desk. We built it because a degree on a CV is still a PDF and a prayer. Cross-border hiring makes that worse: you email a registrar in another country, wait, and often hire before the reply comes, or you pay a background-check vendor to wait for you.

Diploma mills and edited transcripts survive that process. The candidate who actually holds the degree loses the offer to the delay.

We made Gradus a recruiter tool, not a student portal, so an HR lead can post the role's required credentials and track the requisition's fill from the issuer. Authbound Wallet presents the diploma, the transcript, the Erasmus record, and the language certificate. Each row names the institution. A pass is evidence that the ATS can keep. Then you interview. A foreign qualification is no longer a three-week ticket.

(Ask privately for the link to the EUDIW-compatible version)

useCases.title: PulsePay: 148.50 EUR to this shop
useCases.summary:
PulsePay is a fictional merchant payment rail. We built it for demo purposes only for the upcoming EUDI Wallet payment system.

SMS codes get read to a caller. A push that says approve often does not show the payee. The merchant then fights a chargeback with a screenshot. The amount on the screen and the amount that settled are not the same thing.

We made PulsePay a merchant checkout, not an SCA explainer, so an acquirer can walk the tap and see the intent land afterwards. Authbound Wallet signs amount 148.50 EUR, payee Halcyon Cellars Oy, and reference INV-2026-0412. If either the amount or payee changes, that signature is invalid. The sale is a payment the merchant can keep, not a code that has already expired.

useCases.title: Onward: Onboarding - Anna is hired.
useCases.summary:
Onward is a fictional people-ops portal. We built it for the week before a start date, when HR is still chasing scans: identity, right to work, a diploma, a signed contract, an IBAN. Monday arrives, and the laptop is locked because one PDF never came.

An expired licence nobody rechecked is a liability. A contract signed from an email address is a shrug. The hire is already made. The bottleneck is day zero.

We made Onward a checklist, not an HR widget, so a people-ops lead can walk Anna's first day at Valo Construction and see Monday unlock afterwards. Authbound Wallet presents identity, work status, the diploma, a qualified signature on the contract, and a Nordhaus IBAN attestation. The sale is a hire who is actually ready, with evidence HR can keep.

useCases.title: ApteekPlus: The prescription made easy
useCases.summary:
ApteekPlus is a fictional Finnish pharmacy. We built it for the moment at the counter: the medicine is ready, and the pharmacist still has to be sure this is the patient the doctor wrote for.

Paper slips get lost. Screenshots get forwarded. A relative walks in with someone else's printout. Cross-border, the national e-prescription app stays at home. The chain is left holding the liability if the bag goes to the wrong person.

We made ApteekPlus a pharmacy, not a QR widget, so a chain or a health ministry can walk the dispense and see the bag leave with the named patient. Authbound Wallet presents given_name, family_name, document_number, medication, dosage, prescribing_doctor, expiry, and holder_pid. A pass is a signed prescription bound to that holder. The pharmacist dispenses. Nobody printed a slip.

useCases.title: Roamline: Car rental - French licence, Finnish locker, no counter
useCases.summary:
Roamline is a fictional car rental company at Helsinki-Vantaa. We built it for the arrival that has no desk: the car is in a locker, and the company still has to know that this person is licensed to drive it.

A foreign plastic card at a Finnish counter is a judgement call. Designs differ across member states, and the forgeries are good. Unattended pickup cannot photocopy anything. So either you staff a queue, or you skip the check.

We made Roamline a booking site, not a licence widget, so a rental brand can walk the trip and see the locker open afterwards. Authbound Wallet presents document_number, licence_categories, expiry_date, and issuing_country. A French licence can release a Finnish car in the same booking. Valid? The locker code lands before the plane does.

useCases.title: Surepath: Verified humans only
useCases.summary:
Surepath is a fictional dating app. We built it because the inbox is still full of bots, stolen photos, and people who are not the age on the profile. The usual fix is a selfie next to a passport. The app then holds a library of identity images, which is a gift to whoever breaches it, and catfish still get through with a borrowed ID.

We made Surepath a dating product, not an age-check widget, so a product lead can walk the signup and see the badge land afterwards. Authbound is the relying party. Authbound Wallet presents age_over_18, given_name, and nationality. A pass marks the profile a verified human. Unverified accounts cannot see or message that profile. The birthday stays in the wallet. The sale is an adult in the pool, without a drawer of passports.

useCases.title: Civica Vote: one resident, one ballot
useCases.summary:
Civica Vote is a fictional municipal ballot. We built it because participatory budgeting online still fails in two directions: anyone with a second email can vote twice, or the city collects names, and turnout dies.

A bank login names every resident. A paper vote costs a polling station. Cities want the budget decided by people who actually live there, without publishing who backed which fountain.

We made Civica a city ballot, not an eligibility widget, so a municipal team can walk the vote and see a receipt land afterwards. Authbound Wallet presents municipality_of_residence. The DVV population register confirms that the holder lives in Yampere and is 16 or older. The ballot ID is then randomized, so the tally is one resident, one vote, and the city does not keep who picked what. The voter keeps a receipt.
useCases.userJourney:
A Yampere resident opens Civica Vote for the 2026 participatory cycle and marks the ballot (public artwork plus yes/no on city projects).

Casting requires a residency check. They present an Authbound Wallet.

Authbound Wallet shows municipality_of_residence. Value: Yampere. Issuer: DVV Population Register. 16+ and one-ballot are enforced.

The ballot ID is randomized so the vote is unlinked from the person.

Ballot recorded. Receipt 0xA72F · 8C14 · D1. Keep it for audit. It holds no name.

Close the booth. The city publishes the tally after the window closes.

useCases.title: Cartiva: Named Buyer and Named Shop
useCases.summary:
Cartiva is a fictional peer-to-peer marketplace. We built it for the listing that hurts when it goes wrong: a restored Marantz for 480 EUR, shipped across the gulf, paid by someone the seller has never met.

A card and a typed address are still the trust model. First-time buyers ghost. Shops impersonate a real storefront. Escrow holds money but does not know if the buyer is a named adult.

We made Cartiva a product page, not a fraud widget, so a marketplace can walk the purchase and see escrow fill afterwards. Authbound Wallet presents given_name, family_name, age_over_18, and nationality. HiFi Studio Tallinn is already a verified seller. A pass authorizes 480 EUR into Cartiva Trust until delivery. The seller ships to a person, not an inbox. The sale is to a named buyer and a named shop; then the money moves.

useCases.title: Northstay: Hotel - Automatically the locker 412 opens

Northstay is a fictional Helsinki boutique hotel. We built it because Finnish hotels still have to register every guest, and that job still happens as a passport photocopy at the desk, at the hour everyone lands.

The hotel becomes the custodian of travel documents it is not equipped to protect. Night arrivals wait, or they cannot check in at all. Express check-in was a poster until the register was filled.

We made Northstay a hotel, not a KYC widget, so a general manager can walk the arrival and see locker 412 open afterwards. Authbound Wallet presents given_name, family_name, birth_date, and nationality. That is the guest register. The lobby iPad then matches the person standing there to Anna with face scan, and the key compartment opens. The sale to the hotel is a signed record for inspection and no drawer of passports. The desk is optional.

useCases.title: Mandator: Public procurement portal
useCases.summary:
Mandator is a fictional EU public procurement portal. We built it for the question every buyer already has before they open a bid: can this person bind that company?

Today the answer is a stack of PDFs. A registry extract, a board resolution, a power of attorney, often in a language the contracting authority does not read, and rarely rechecked before countersigning. A procurement lead either waits for the CEO or the bid goes unsigned.

We made Mandator a tender desk, not a mandate widget, so a contracting authority can walk a submission and see the company seal land afterwards. Authbound is the relying party. Matti Virtanen, CEO of Valo Construction Oy, signs a power of attorney into Authbound Wallet once. Anna Example, procurement lead, carries it: submit tenders up to 5M EUR, valid through 31 Dec 2026. Each bid then ships with a Qualified eSeal. The buyer sees authority, not a zip file of scans.

useCases.title: Jevi WorkPass: Operations console
useCases.summary:
Jevi WorkPass is a fictional municipal operations console for a construction site. We built it because the gate still runs on a folder: licences, medicals, hot-work tickets, photocopied, often expired, and checked by a person who has forty others waiting.

A welder with no height medical still walks onto the span. The investigation then finds the binder. Revoking a ticket means calling every supervisor.

We made WorkPass a crew board, not a certificate widget, so a site manager can walk the morning and see the gate open only when the proofs are current. Authbound Wallet presents given_name, family_name, role, competence_certificate, medical_clearance, and substance_free. Elina Nummi sits on Proof needed until that scan. A pass clears her. The sale to the municipality is a gate that fails before anyone climbs, and a roster that is not a shared drive of scans.

useCases.title: Aurora Bet: KYC for online gambling
useCases.summary:
Aurora Bet is a fictional sportsbook and casino. The licence still needs a named adult on the account before the first deposit. An over-18 gate (wine, cigarettes) is not enough here. The operator also needs to know who the player is and from which member state.

That check is where live operators lose signups. Aurora Bet is the full front door: live tables, jackpots, create-account, lobby. The player confirms in Authbound Wallet. The floor opens, the welcome bonus lands, and verified withdrawals unlock.

Authbound Wallet is the holder. Requested claims: given_name, family_name, nationality, age_over_18.
